guide.title: Monitoring Devices
guide.lead: Monitors extend your senses but they can lie. Look at the waveform before you trust the number, and treat the patient, not the screen. Capnography and glucose are two of the most useful checks you have.

groups.title: Reads falsely normal
items: Carbon monoxide: binds hemoglobin about 200–250 times more strongly than oxygen

groups.title: Do
items: Check the waveform; warm the hand; try the ear
Match it with the patient's colour, breathing and mental status

sections.title: Read the capnograph
rows: Tube out or no circulation: check now

sections.title: Cardiac monitor leads
notes: AHA: "white on right, smoke over fire".
A rhythm strip can't rule out a STEMI: record a 12-lead within 10 minutes for chest pain.

sections.title: Glucose
items: Check in altered mental status, seizures, stroke symptoms, diabetes
A normal reading hours ago doesn't rule out a low now

quiz.q: SpO₂ 92% with cold, pale hands, weak radial pulse and a poor waveform. Best action?
options: Warm the hand, try the earlobe, match with clinical signs
quiz.explanation: Trust the waveform, then the number.

quiz.q: During CPR, EtCO₂ jumps from 12 to 42 mmHg:
quiz.explanation: Check for a pulse at the next pause.

quiz.q: Asthmatic using accessory muscles, 2-word sentences, EtCO₂ 52 mmHg with a shark-fin waveform:
options: Bronchospasm with CO₂ retention: tiring, may need assisted ventilation
quiz.explanation: High EtCO₂ in asthma is a danger sign.

options: A rhythm the AED calls "shock advised"

quiz.q: Smoke-inhalation patient: SpO₂ 98%, headache, confusion. Why be cautious?
options: Carbon monoxide makes SpO₂ falsely normal
The sensor is always wrong in men

quiz.q: IEC colour for the right-arm electrode:
Can a 3-lead rhythm strip rule out a STEMI?
Flat capnography line just after intubation:
options: Tube displaced or no circulation: check immediately

flashcards.question: Shark-fin capnography waveform
flashcards.answer: Bronchospasm: air trapping in asthma or COPD.

flashcards.question: Most important reason to check glucose
flashcards.answer: Altered mental status of unknown cause: hypoglycemia is quick to reverse.

flashcards.question: Sudden EtCO₂ rise during CPR
flashcards.answer: Probable ROSC: cardiac output is carrying CO₂ back to the lungs.

flashcards.question: Limb lead colours
flashcards.answer: AHA: white right arm, black left arm, red left leg ("white on right, smoke over fire"). IEC: red right arm, yellow left arm, green left leg.

flashcards.question: Carbon monoxide and SpO₂
flashcards.answer: The oximeter reads carboxyhemoglobin as oxygenated: SpO₂ looks normal while the patient is hypoxic.

flashcards.question: EtCO₂ during CPR
flashcards.answer: Below 10 mmHg suggests poor compressions: check depth, rate and recoil.

critical.scenario: Rescued from a smoke-filled room after 10 minutes: confused, coughing, headache. SpO₂ 98% on a non-rebreather with a good waveform; pink, warm skin.
critical.question: Most critical concern?

options.t: Carbon monoxide poisoning with falsely normal SpO₂: keep 100% oxygen, monitor, transport

options.f: Confusion after smoke is poisoning until proven otherwise.

critical.explanation: Synthetic materials also raise the risk of cyanide.

critical.scenario: A 68-year-old with heart failure and COPD on a non-rebreather: SpO₂ 91%, shark-fin waveform, EtCO₂ rising from 46 to 54 mmHg over 8 minutes, getting drowsier.
critical.question: Next action?

options.t: Respiratory failure with CO₂ retention and falling consciousness: assist ventilation with a BVM, titrate oxygen to 88–92%, call ALS and prepare for advanced airway support
options.f: Correct. CPAP/NIV is only for patients awake enough to protect their airway.
Rising CO₂ and drowsiness mean failure.
More oxygen can worsen CO₂ retention.

critical.explanation: The trend matters more than any one number. Had she been alert and protecting her airway, CPAP/NIV would be an option.

critical.scenario: A 78-year-old diabetic on insulin skipped breakfast and is more confused. Glucose now 48 mg/dL. Staff insist it was 132 two hours ago.
critical.question: Interpretation and action?

options.t: The current reading is valid: treat the hypoglycemia (oral glucose if he can swallow safely, otherwise glucagon) and transport

critical.explanation: Insulin without food drops glucose quickly.
